Service-Level Commitments During Warehouse Disruptions: • Proactive customer notification within 4 hours of confirmed impact to ship date, including scope, ETA, and remediation plan (DOC‑SLA‑001 §2.3); • Interim status updates at least every 24 hours until resolution (DOC‑SLA‑001 §§2.3–2.4); • Apply SLA remedies for missed ship dates per section 2.4 and record affected orders for credit/refund processing (DOC‑SLA‑001 §2.4); • Prioritize enterprise/high‑touch accounts for direct, expedited communications as specified in §2.3.  
Incident Classification & Escalation for Fulfillment Issues: • Severity 1 — site outage/critical stoppage (broad order impact): incident declared and incident commander/ops mobilize within 15 minutes; notify Director_of_Operations and Customer Success and engage customer‑facing teams within 30 minutes (Service Disruption Playbook v2.0 §3.1); • Severity 2 — partial capacity loss or targeted backlog affecting key SKUs/customers: escalate to regional ops lead within 1 hour; coordinate mitigation and notify account teams with status cadence every 2–4 hours (Playbook §3.2); • Severity 3 — minor delays or isolated exceptions: managed by site manager with daily monitoring and customer teams notified only if individual SLAs will be missed (Playbook §3.3).  
All items above are drawn directly from DOC‑SLA‑001 (§§2.3–2.4) and Service Disruption Playbook v2.0 (§§3.1–3.3) and reflect the documented timelines and escalation triggers.

Customer Communication Expectations During Warehouse Disruptions: • Notify affected customers within 4 hours of confirmed ship‑date impact, including scope, affected orders, revised ETA, and remediation plan; • Provide formal status updates at least every 24 hours until resolution (or more frequently if severity escalates); • Disclose SLA remedies (credits/refunds) and next‑update timing in communications; • Route account‑level outreach through Customer Success/account teams and prioritize enterprise/high‑touch customers (DOC‑SLA‑001 §§2.3–2.5; DOC‑IM‑04 stakeholder comms).

rounds.response:
Key Takeaways for Leadership on Warehouse Disruptions and Customer Impact:
• Service-level rules require initial customer notification within 4 hours of confirmed ship‑date impact and formal status updates at least every 24 hours until resolution; SLA remedies for missed ship dates are applied per DOC‑SLA‑001 (§§2.3–2.4).  
• Incidents are classified and escalated per the playbook with Severity 1 mobilization (incident commander within ~15 minutes; notify Director_of_Operations and Customer Success within ~30 minutes) and defined timelines for Severity 2/3 (DOC‑IM‑04; Service Disruption Playbook).  
• The risk register and PIRs document primary customer impacts as delivery delays/missed windows, order cancellations/modifications, split shipments/backorders, and issuance of credits/refunds (DOC‑RSK‑12 §4; PIRs).  
• Post‑incident reviews consistently show secondary effects that affect customers: spikes in support/contact volume, longer case handle times and repeat contacts, and increased manual remediation (expedites/reroutes/manual picks) that raise error risk and processing time.  
• Leadership should expect executive incident summaries and status packs that surface: affected order counts and % of volume impacted, SLA breach/missed‑ship counts, customer support/escalation volumes, credits/refunds issued or pending, and current fulfillment capacity with estimated time‑to‑recovery (DOC‑IM‑04; PIRs).  
Sources: DOC‑SLA‑001 (§§2.3–2.5), DOC‑IM‑04 (incident management/stakeholder comms), DOC‑RSK‑12 §4, and recent full‑site/multi‑site PIRs.
